# maisongr-law25

> An open-source npm package (MIT, no runtime dependencies, Node 20.9+) that keeps a Québec Law 25 privacy impact assessment (évaluation des facteurs relatifs à la vie privée, EFVP) in a project's repository, checks it against the project's schema in CI (Prisma, Drizzle, TypeORM, Sequelize, Mongoose, Django, SQLAlchemy, Rails, Laravel, Entity Framework, JPA/Hibernate, GORM, SQL migrations, OpenAPI or JSON Schema), and writes the report in French and English. Not legal advice; it doesn't determine whether an assessment is required or sufficient.

## Use it

- `npx maisongr-law25 init`: writes law25.config.mjs with one item per schema field that looks personal, and TODO placeholders.
- `npx maisongr-law25 check`: exit 1 when a TODO is left, a text is missing in a language, a provider outside Québec (the rest of Canada counts) has no s. 17 assessment, the next review date has passed, or a schema field that looks personal (by name, or a `@personal` comment) is in no item's `fields` and not in `notPersonal`. `--json` for a machine-readable result; `--github` for GitHub Actions annotations (a missing field on its schema line).
- Without code: GitHub Action `uses: maison-gr/maisongr-law25@v1.0.3` (inputs command check|build, working-directory, config, schema, stack, args, version); pre-commit hook `maisongr-law25`; Docker `docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/work" ghcr.io/maison-gr/maisongr-law25 check`.
- `npx maisongr-law25 build`: docs/privacy/efvp.fr.md and docs/privacy/pia.en.md.
- Schema sources, found by themselves in this order: a Prisma schema; the models of every ORM the code uses (Drizzle, TypeORM, MikroORM, sequelize-typescript, NestJS Mongoose, Sequelize, Mongoose, Django, SQLAlchemy, SQLModel, Rails, Laravel, Entity Framework, JPA/Hibernate in Java or Kotlin, GORM), read together; SQL migrations (supabase/migrations, migrations, db/migrations); an OpenAPI or JSON Schema file. Dependency, build and test folders are skipped. `--schema <path>` (repeatable) with `--stack <name>` reads given paths; `--prisma` / `--sql` still work; `--no-schema` checks the assessment alone.
- Markers: a `@personal` or `@not-personal` comment in the language's syntax, or `x-personal: true|false` in OpenAPI and JSON Schema.
- Every text is a string or `{ fr, en }`. `source` is person, third-party, generated or public. Risk `stage` is collection, use, communication, retention or other; `status` is done, planned or to-confirm.

## When a field holding personal information is added

Add it to an item's `fields` in law25.config.mjs, with whose it is, its purpose and its retention, or create a new item. If it goes to a provider outside Québec, the provider's `transfer` covers it. If it is not personal, add it to `notPersonal` with the reason. Ask a person to confirm the purpose and retention: they are the organisation's decisions.
